     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# @file resolve-threads.sh
     3	# @brief Reply to a PR's unresolved review threads with the orchestrator's dispositions and resolve them.
     4	# @description
     5	#   Plan 021 step 6.3, the chain step behind the ruleset's required_review_thread_resolution. One GraphQL query
     6	#   reads the first 100 review threads of the PR. Each unresolved thread is keyed on its first comment's database
     7	#   id, and its disposition is the row of the table whose first column is that id, else, when a sweep JSON is given,
     8	#   the `disposition` of the sweep item whose `url` ends with `_r<id>`. A `fixed:` or `not-applicable:` disposition
     9	#   gets one reply in its fixed sentence, the disposition in backticks as fill_sweep.py reads a reply back, and one
    10	#   resolveReviewThread mutation, the thread id passed as a GraphQL variable; the thread counts as resolved only when
    11	#   the mutation answers `isResolved` true. A thread without a disposition, with another form, or not answered true
    12	#   is reported and left open. `--dry-run` prints what would be done and writes nothing. gh runs with the
    13	#   orchestrator's credentials, so this runs outside the sandbox.
    14	# @arg $1 int PR number.
    15	# @arg $2 path The disposition table: TSV rows of a comment id and its disposition.
    16	# @arg $3 string `--dry-run`, or any placeholder such as `-`.
    17	# @arg $4 path The sweep JSON (optional).
    18	# @exitcode 0 Every unresolved thread was resolved (under `--dry-run`, would be).
    19	# @exitcode 2 Usage error.
    20	# @exitcode 3 A thread has no disposition, one of another form, or a resolve answer other than true; it is left open.
    21	# @example
    22	#   scripts/orchestrator/resolve-threads.sh 355 extra.tsv - .orchestration/validation/t-a01-pr-feedback.json
    23	set -euo pipefail
    24	
    25	usage() {
    26	    echo "usage: resolve-threads.sh <pr> <extra.tsv> [--dry-run|-] [<sweep.json>]" >&2
    27	    exit 2
    28	}
    29	(($# >= 2 && $# <= 4)) || usage
    30	pr=$1 tsv=$2 dry=${3:-} sweep=${4:-}
    31	[[ ${pr} =~ ^[0-9]+$ && -f ${tsv} ]] || usage
    32	query="query { repository(owner:\"mryfmo\", name:\"dotfiles\") { pullRequest(number:${pr}) { reviewThreads(first:100) \
    33	{ nodes { id isResolved comments(first:1) { nodes { databaseId } } } } } } }"
    34	threads=$(gh api graphql -f query="${query}" --jq '.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[] | select(.isResolved|not) | "\(.comments.nodes[0].databaseId) \(.id)"')
    35	# The thread id travels as a GraphQL variable, never inside the query text.
    36	# shellcheck disable=SC2016 # $threadId is GraphQL's variable, not the shell's
    37	resolve='mutation ($threadId: ID!) { resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: $threadId}) { thread { isResolved } } }'
    38	missing=0 resolved=0
    39	# The threads come in on fd 3, so a command in the loop that reads stdin cannot swallow the rest of them.
    40	while read -r cid tid <&3; do
    41	    [[ -n ${cid} ]] || continue
    42	    row=$(awk -F'\t' -v id="${cid}" '$1 == id {print $2; exit}' "${tsv}")
    43	    if [[ -z ${row} && -s ${sweep} ]]; then
    44	        row=$(jq -r --arg suffix "_r${cid}" \
    45	            'first(.items[] | select((.url // "") | endswith($suffix)) | .disposition // "") // ""' "${sweep}")
    46	    fi
    47	    if [[ -z ${row} ]]; then
    48	        echo "no disposition row for thread ${cid} (table or sweep); left open"
    49	        missing=1
    50	        continue
    51	    fi
    52	    case ${row} in
    53	    fixed:*)
    54	        body="Disposition (orchestrator): \`${row}\`. Fixed at root cause in that commit on this branch; verified by \
    55	the task's tests and CI on the final head. Resolving."
    56	        ;;
    57	    not-applicable:*) body="Disposition (orchestrator): \`${row}\`. Resolving; the owning task on main carries it." ;;
    58	    *)
    59	        echo "row for ${cid} has an unknown form: ${row}"
    60	        missing=1
    61	        continue
    62	        ;;
    63	    esac
    64	    if [[ ${dry} == --dry-run ]]; then
    65	        echo "would reply+resolve ${cid}: ${row:0:90}"
    66	        continue
    67	    fi
    68	    gh api -X POST "repos/mryfmo/dotfiles/pulls/${pr}/comments/${cid}/replies" -f body="${body}" --jq '.id' > /dev/null
    69	    state=$(gh api graphql -f query="${resolve}" -f threadId="${tid}" --jq '.data.resolveReviewThread.thread.isResolved')
    70	    if [[ ${state} != true ]]; then
    71	        echo "thread ${cid} not resolved (isResolved: ${state:-none}); left open"
    72	        missing=1
    73	        continue
    74	    fi
    75	    resolved=$((resolved + 1))
    76	    echo "resolved ${cid} (${row:0:60})"
    77	done 3<<< "${threads}"
    78	echo "resolved ${resolved} thread(s); missing rows: ${missing}"
    79	[[ ${missing} == 0 ]] || exit 3

   186	"""Apply each mutant alone as a literal replacement (asserted to match once), run its test, restore with git checkout.
   187	
   188	Prints one `mutant <n> rc=<test status> <file>: <label> (<test>)` line per mutant (caught is rc=1), then a baseline.
   189	"""
   190	
   191	import subprocess
   192	import sys
   193	from pathlib import Path
   194	
   195	H = "tests.unit.test_herdr_agents.HerdrAgentsTest."
   196	I = "tests.unit.test_integration_seat.IntegrationSeatTest."
   197	CAP = H + "test_add_worker_refuses_a_seat_beyond_the_manifest_worker_cap"
   198	TEXT = H + "test_the_skill_and_the_rule_name_the_manifest_worker_cap_and_the_integration_seat"
   199	CHAIN = I + "test_integrate_seat_runs_the_steps_in_order_stops_at_the_first_failure_and_never_merges"
   200	COLOUR = I + "test_integrate_seat_reads_plain_gh_output_under_clicolor_force"
   201	PRE = I + "test_result_precheck_refuses_each_missing_condition_and_verify_refuses_a_result_without_a_matching_receipt"
   202	HA = "home/dot_local/bin/common/executable_herdr-agents"
   203	SEAT, PC = "scripts/orchestrator/integrate-seat.sh", "scripts/orchestrator/result-precheck.sh"
   204	MUTANTS = [
   205	    (HA, 'if [[ ${seat_seated} == false ]] && ((seats >= seat_cap)); then', "if false; then", "the cap check dropped", CAP),
   206	    (HA, "((seats >= seat_cap))", "((seats > seat_cap))", "the cap off by one", CAP),
   207	    ("home/dot_agents/skills/agmsg-orchestration/SKILL.md", "(4 in the manifest today) in total", "(3 in the manifest today) in total", "a seat count out of step", TEXT),
   208	    ("home/dot_config/claude/rules/agmsg-orchestration.md", "the rest of integration runs on the integration seat through", "the rest of integration runs on another seat through", "the Delegation bullet without the integration seat", TEXT),
   209	    (SEAT, "export CLICOLOR_FORCE=0 FORCE_COLOR=0 NO_COLOR=1", "export FORCE_COLOR=0 NO_COLOR=1", "CLICOLOR_FORCE inherited", COLOUR),
   210	    (SEAT, '[[ ${ok} == *",${rc},"* ]] || {', "true || {", "a failing step does not block", CHAIN),
   211	    (SEAT, "elif [[ ${p} == P[23] && -n ${owner} ]]; then", "elif [[ -n ${owner} ]]; then", "an unfixed P0/P1 made advisory", CHAIN),
   212	    (PC, "[[ ${f} != ${g} ]] || hit=yes", "hit=yes", "(b) takes any file", PRE),
   213	    (PC, "exit !(o <= max && t <= tmax)", "exit 0", "(c) ignores the caps", PRE),
   214	    (PC, '/usr/bin/grep -q -F -- "${c}" "${d}/validation.md" || bad=1', 'true || bad=1', "(d) ignores the validation file", PRE),
   215	    (PC, '[ "$(gh pr view "${pr}" --json headRefOid --jq .headRefOid)" = "${head}" ] && gh pr checks', "gh pr checks", "(e) not bound to the head", PRE),
   216	    (PC, '/usr/bin/grep -q -E "${id}:${p}:$([[ ${p} == P[01] ]] && echo \'(fixed:[0-9a-f]{7}|open:)\')" "${d}/report.md" || bad=1', '/usr/bin/grep -q -F "${id}" "${d}/report.md" || bad=1', "(g) takes any mention of the id", PRE),
   217	    (PC, 'miss+="code-after-receipt,"', ":", "verify takes code after the receipt", PRE),
   218	    (PC, '[ "${want#task_sha256=}" = "$(shasum -a 256 < "${d}/task.md" | cut -d\' \' -f1)" ]', "true", "(a) takes any task copy", PRE),
   219	]
   220	
   221	
   222	def test(name):
   223	    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "unittest", name], capture_output=True, text=True).returncode
   224	
   225	
   226	for n, (rel, old, new, label, name) in enumerate(MUTANTS, 1):
   227	    path = Path(rel)
   228	    text = path.read_text()
   229	    assert text.count(old) == 1, (rel, label, text.count(old))
   230	    path.write_text(text.replace(old, new))
   231	    rc = test(name)
   232	    subprocess.run(["git", "checkout", "--", rel], check=True)
   233	    print(f"mutant {n} rc={rc} {rel}: {label} ({name.rsplit('.', 1)[1]})", flush=True)
   234	names = list(dict.fromkeys(name for *_, name in MUTANTS))
   235	rc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "unittest", *names], capture_output=True, text=True).returncode
   236	print(f"baseline rc={rc}: the {len(names)} tests on the unmutated tree")

 succeeded in 261ms:

RESULT reports must mark durable facts with the same CompactionDB marker contract. In CompactionDB-opted-in projects, the worker runs `uv run --no-project .claude/hooks/contextdb_cli.py memory add` before completion and includes the exact command or commands in the RESULT report.

RESULT validation files must contain the verbatim output of every validation command actually executed — not summaries or PASS labels alone — and any identifier the report claims to have created (commit hash, PR number, CompactionDB memory/decision ID) must appear in that pasted output. A claim without its pasted output is treated as unexecuted and grounds for `status=revise`.

`AGMSG-ACCEPTANCE v1` fields:

```text
AGMSG-ACCEPTANCE v1 task_id=<id> status=accepted|revise reason=<short-reason> next_action=<action>
```

Each acceptance record also includes a `cost:` line with worker-reported token/cost figures when available, otherwise `cost: n/a`.

A RESULT with a P0/P1 surviving the one worker-side fix round carries `bot_rounds=2` and lists it as `open:<thread id>` (`open:review-<review id>` for a review-body finding); the PR stops for the operator's decision (Worker Playbook step 15). A `status=revise` ACCEPTANCE carries `previous_head=<the RESULT head being revised>` and one failing-test selector per finding (`check=tests/<file>::<name>`); the worker records both in `.orchestration/<task id>/revise.yaml`, beside the task.md copy.

Liveness messages:

```text
AGMSG-PING v1 task_id=<id> reason=<short-reason>
AGMSG-PONG v1 task_id=<id> status=alive|blocked|question note=<short-note>
```

`question`: the worker holds and asks; INV-6 counts it.

## `.orchestration` Workspace Layout

- `tasks/`: orchestrator-authored task specs.
- `reports/`: worker reports and blocked-task reports.
- `validation/`: command output and validation evidence.
- `acceptance/`: orchestrator acceptance, revision, or rejection records.
- `sandboxes/`: per-task isolation records (sandbox/worktree evidence).

```text
AGMSG-TASK v1 task_id=<id> repo=<absolute-repo-path> task_file=<path>
allowed_files=<paths-or-see-task-file-section> forbidden_actions=<semicolon-list>
expected_result_file=<path> expected_validation_file=<path>
expected_sandbox_file=<path> expected_learning_file=<path>
expected_autoskill_file=<path> done_signal=AGMSG-RESULT max_turns=<n>
note=act-as-worker-<task-or-role>
```

Task files must state durable facts with `[memory:decision]` or `[memory:failure]` markers using the tag form, bracket form, and kind aliases defined by the vendored CompactionDB README.

`AGMSG-RESULT v1` fields:

```text
AGMSG-RESULT v1 task_id=<id> status=ready_for_review|blocked
report=<path> validation=<path> sandbox=<path> learning=<path> autoskill=<path>
```

Tasks that create persistent side effects outside the repository working tree, such as global asset installs, writes under `$HOME`, or external service registrations, include the optional field `effects=<semicolon-list-of-short-ids>`. In-repository edits within `allowed_files` are not effects. For each declared effect, the report must state its reverse mapping: a named `~/.agents/.installed-manifest.json` step removable with `remove-agent-asset`, a documented removal procedure, or an `irreversible:` statement with rationale.

RESULT reports must mark durable facts with the same CompactionDB marker contract. In CompactionDB-opted-in projects, the worker runs `uv run --no-project .claude/hooks/contextdb_cli.py memory add` before completion and includes the exact command or commands in the RESULT report.

# Learning triage: dotfiles-T129-integration-seat-result-gate-cap-a01

These are candidates only; nothing is promoted.

1. [memory:failure] Under `set -euo pipefail`, `x="$(sed … "${missing_file}" 2> /dev/null | head -n 1)"` exits the script: the failed `sed` fails the pipeline and the assignment. A read of an optional file needs `|| x=''`, and its test needs the absent-file case, which the existing add-worker tests supplied here.
2. [memory:failure] A loop that checks items with `cmd && [ ok ]` as its last command reports only the last item's status; an earlier failing item is hidden. Collect a failure flag (`|| bad=1`) and return it.
3. [memory:decision] `git rebase --no-gpg-sign` rebases on this host, where `-c commit.gpgsign=false rebase` still fails its commit step with `failed to write commit object`.
4. [memory:decision] macOS `/bin/bash` 3.2 has no `mapfile`, and test suites that put `/usr/bin:/bin` first run scripts with it; read lines into an array with a `while read` loop and expand it as `${a[@]+"${a[@]}"}`.

    62	Written 2026-10-17 by the orchestrator seat as plan 023's PR F2. Three PRs of the day fixed one path-form at a time (#379: an encoded tilde, a logical cwd, a bare tilde, a trailing slash, an encoded separator) or one process-form at a time (#383: a truncated ps line, a hidden process); the operator withdrew the template sentence that would have asked humans to remember and asked for a check instead. Round 2 of this text applies the Codex half's six findings: no `make lint` exists and none is added (the lint is a unit test under `make unit-test`, which the test workflow runs for every diff the lint covers: premises 1 and 2); the four hits on origin/main sit in files that in-flight PRs own, so a content-hashed baseline carries them and a stale row fails (premise 3); item 1 is a rule table with one fixture per rule; Python comparisons are read from the `ast`; no workflow is in allowed_files.
    63	
    64	## Goal
    65	
    66	`make unit-test` fails when a shell, Python or jq expression in a tracked file under `home/`, `scripts/` or `install/` compares a path, URL or process by its string form instead of through a normaliser, unless the line is in the baseline or carries an allow marker with a reason.
    67	
    68	## Files
    69	
    70	1. `scripts/lint-comparisons.py` (new; standard library only; `python3 -I scripts/lint-comparisons.py [--list-rules] [--baseline <tsv>] [<file>...]`; the default file set is `git ls-files -z -- home scripts install` filtered to names ending in `.sh`, `.bash`, `.zsh`, `.py` or `.tmpl` or whose first line is a `sh`, `bash`, `zsh` or `python` shebang). An operand is a path, URL or process operand when it is a literal containing `/`, `~`, `file://`, `.html` or `%2F`, or a variable, parameter or attribute whose name, split into segments at `_`, `.`, `-` and lower-to-upper case changes, has a segment equal (case-insensitive) to `path`, `url`, `cwd`, `dir`, `root`, `file`, `home`, `pid` or `proc`, or to one of those followed by `s` (`file_path`, `before_urls`, `baseDir` match; `profile_hash`, `EXCLUDED_DIR_NAMES`'s `DIR` matches, `filename` and `director` do not): a segment match, never a substring match (Amendment 1). Each hit is printed as `<file>:<line>: <rule id> <rule text>` and the exit status is 1 when any hit is outside the baseline; a hit is accepted when the same statement wraps the operand in a normaliser of its row's Allowed column, or the line carries `# lint-comparisons: allow <reason>` (jq: `# lint-comparisons: allow <reason>` on the shell line that holds the jq program). The rules:

    72	| id | forbidden form | allowed normalisers | fixture (refused) |
    73	|----|----------------|---------------------|-------------------|
    74	| R0 | the marker `# lint-comparisons: allow` without a reason after it | a reason of at least one word | `[[ $a == $b ]] # lint-comparisons: allow` |

    76	| R2 | shell `case <path or URL operand> in` | the same as R1 | `case "$url" in file://*) ;; esac` |
    77	| R3 | jq `==`, `!=`, `startswith(`, `endswith(`, `ltrimstr(`, `rtrimstr(` or `test(` whose operand is `.url`, `.path`, a `$name` of the token rule or a literal of the token rule | a jq `def canonical_path`, `def normalise_*` or `def normalize_*` applied to both sides | `select(.url \| endswith("/index.html"))` |
    78	| R4 | Python `ast.Compare` with `Eq`, `NotEq`, `In` or `NotIn`, and `ast.Call` of `.startswith` or `.endswith`, where an operand is an `ast.Name` or `ast.Attribute` of the token rule or an `ast.Constant` string containing `/` | the operand is an `ast.Call` of `os.path.realpath`, `os.path.normpath`, `os.path.abspath`, `Path(...).resolve`, `urllib.parse.urlsplit`, `urlparse`, `unquote`, `canonical_path`, `normalise_*` or `normalize_*`, or the comparison is `os.path.samefile` | `if path == "/x":` |
    79	| R5 | a process read as text: `ps` piped to `grep`, `awk`, `cut` or `sed`, or `pgrep -f` with a pattern that is a variable | `ps -o <fields>= -p <pid>` (one pid, named fields) or `pgrep -x <name>` | `ps -axo pid,command \| grep claude` |
    80	| R6 | an identifier interpolated into a regex: `grep -E` whose pattern contains `${name}` or `$name` unescaped, `re.compile`, `re.search`, `re.match` or `re.fullmatch` on an f-string | `grep -F`, a pattern built with a function named `escape_regex`, or `re.escape(name)` inside the f-string | `grep -E "^(${ids})\t"` |

Audited [PR #393](https://github.com/mryfmo/dotfiles/pull/393) at `9c07098147d3b16d68a9be2772fbcba2460b8851`. Modified nothing.

- [P1] high implementation `scripts/orchestrator/result-precheck.sh:33` — Missing or nonexistent receipt `head:` values pass verification: `git diff` fails, but `|| true` converts the failure into an empty comparison. Reproduced with the verifier block.
- [P1] high implementation `scripts/orchestrator/result-precheck.sh:33` — The artifact exemption matches substrings, accepting later executable changes such as `src/.orchestration/<task>/code.sh`; it must match the repository-root directory.
- [P1] high implementation `scripts/orchestrator/result-precheck.sh:31` — Verification permits `unavailable` for mandatory checks (a)–(g), although only (h) and (i) allow it; a receipt marking all nine unavailable passes.
- [P1] high implementation `scripts/orchestrator/result-precheck.sh:51` — Check (a) hashes the working-tree task copy instead of the copy at the supplied head; restored local metadata can conceal a different committed task and influence checks (b)–(d).
- [P1] high implementation `scripts/orchestrator/integrate-seat.sh:33` — RESULT consumption never invokes receipt verification, and no production caller invokes `result-precheck.sh`; missing or rejected receipts therefore do not mechanically prevent integration.
- [P1] high implementation `scripts/orchestrator/integrate-seat.sh:24` — HEAD equality does not establish trusted executable contents: modified integration dependencies can run despite the checkout pointing at `origin/main`.
- [P1] high implementation `scripts/orchestrator/integrate-seat.sh:33` — Finding-free RESULTs without `threads=` are rejected, while `threads=none` and `threads=-` fail the parser at line 95; the normal no-findings path cannot complete.
- [P1] high orchestration `.orchestration/acceptance/dotfiles-T129-integration-seat-result-gate-cap-a01.md:60` — D-F4-round3 authorizes a third fix round despite the incorporated two-round cap and recorded S2 thresholds; no qualifying redesign/reset or operator waiver is supplied.
- [P2] high implementation `scripts/orchestrator/integrate-seat.sh:93` — Dispositions use only the earlier RESULT’s thread list; findings arriving during the Bot wait are absent, so even an advisory P2 with `--owner` blocks resolution instead of receiving the specified disposition.
- [P2] high implementation `scripts/orchestrator/integrate-seat.sh:100` — Bot advisory dispositions neither verify that the owner task exists nor add ownership/class rows to acceptance; threads can be resolved against nonexistent ownership and leave incomplete gate evidence.
- [P2] high implementation `scripts/orchestrator/result-precheck.sh:76` — Command-name presence substitutes for execution evidence: bare commands or failed transcripts satisfy check (d) without the required validation output.
- [P2] high implementation `scripts/orchestrator/result-precheck.sh:92` — Check (g) accepts unresolved P0/P1 `open:` tokens without `bot_rounds=2`, and accepts empty P2 dispositions; both bypass explicit readiness requirements.
- [P2] high implementation `scripts/orchestrator/result-precheck.sh:87` — Review-body findings are never enumerated, so an omitted review-body P0/P1 still yields an `ok` precheck; advisory ownership does not make this behavior correct.
- [P2] high specification `.orchestration/tasks/dotfiles-T129-integration-seat-result-gate-cap-a01.md:41` — The input trust boundary remains declared `closed`, although its named test omits the demonstrated receipt bypasses and the acknowledged review-body gap.
- [P2] high conformance `.orchestration/dotfiles-T129-integration-seat-result-gate-cap-a01/report.md:56` — The recorded revise round has no committed `revise.yaml`, despite the Message Contract requiring its previous head and check selectors alongside `task.md`.
- [P2] high conformance `.orchestration/sandboxes/dotfiles-T129-integration-seat-result-gate-cap-a01.md:19` — Tests and the entire receipt-producing precheck were run unsandboxed as claimed step-4 exceptions; that procedure does not exempt those operations, and no task-specific override is documented.
